Later turn-ons use Save settings like every other toggle and open no modal. A page of its own under Administration > Service, like Labor Rates and Canned Lines. Two tabs. The starting set is seeded when the setting is first turned on: General Internal (the default) here, Warranty, Goodwill and Comeback on the other tab. The QuickBooks column shows the expense account for the location you are in, as the parts Categories page shows Products and Services; Not set means ShopView Review until one is picked. The shop adds its own (Company Vehicle Maintenance, Shop Equipment Maintenance) or archives what it does not use. The same accounts are also editable in Integrations > QuickBooks > ShopView Accounts, one row per category, for shops used to mapping there (frame 9). Same page, second tab. The third column says whether the category requires the original work order (Warranty and Comeback do). Several categories can share an account. New No Charge Category, or a click on a row (Edit). Name, the QuickBooks expense account per connected location (one small table, so a multi-location shop sets everything here) and whether the category requires the original work order. Nothing is created in QuickBooks: the account is picked from the chart that is already there. Archive is in the row menu; a category is never deleted, so old work orders and reports keep it. The badge is the only change on this page. Search finds the flagged customer by name. The checkbox is the only place the flag is set. Save flags the customer; when it already has open billable work orders the dialog of frame 7 follows. Shown only while the setting is on. Not shown on New Customer. Only the last field is new, and only on assets of an internal customer. Priority on a new internal work order: the asset's category, else the customer's default, else General Internal. Leave it empty on vehicles; set it on equipment and buildings that sit under the same internal customer. Same mapping, second door: one row per category under Cost of Parts, grouped Internal work orders and No Charge work orders. Editing here or on the category writes the same value for this location; a new category adds its row here by itself. Cost of Parts and Inventory Asset are used as today for the credit side. Clicks Create Work Order. Staging Heavy Duty Fleet is an internal customer, so the work order is internal: Internal badge, no checkbox, no category to pick. The tooltip says where it posts (the asset's category, else the customer's, else General Internal). Nobody on the work order is asked an accounting question. Forklift 2 carries its own internal category (Flow 0 frame 11b), so the tooltip now names Shop Equipment Maintenance, from the asset. Change it on the asset, not here. Opens the Finance tab. Returns to Lines after the technicians mark every line Complete. Clicks Close Work Order. One press, like Create invoice: completes and closes. One success alert at the top; X dismisses it, then the locked note shows as on any closed work order. Same Finance tab and toolbar as today. The invoice number is the work order number and the document is stamped NO CHARGE. No Add Deposit, Create Invoice, Remit payment to or balance due. Downloads the invoice from the toolbar, then returns to the Work Orders list. On the document the stamp and the category line sit under the masthead line, left, clear of the logo that prints in the top centre. Closed work orders show where invoiced ones show (All tab, Status chip), not in Completed, which lists work waiting for an invoice. Category is required when No Charge is ticked and starts empty; Save says Pick a category until one is picked. The list holds the shop's active No Charge categories (Warranty, Goodwill, Comeback to start). Warranty and Comeback also show Original work order: the customer's earlier work orders, same asset first, and Not in ShopView. Optional here, required at Close. New: an optional Original line select under the original work order; the line sets the original technician for the comeback and warranty numbers (else the lead technician of the original work order). Shown while the setting is on and the work order is not invoiced; needs Work Orders Create & Edit and See Financial Data, like fees and discounts. Clicks Convert to No Charge. New: an optional Original line select under the original work order; the line sets the original technician for the comeback and warranty numbers (else the lead technician of the original work order). The category shows on the NO CHARGE document and in the report, not on the work order. Every change of classification writes a system note on the work order and an Audit Log entry: Convert to No Charge (category, original work order, what was removed), Change category, Convert to Billable, Close and Reopen. Notes are read-only and carry who and when. Opened from the menu (Change category). Save is enabled once the category or the original work order differs from the current one. Convert to Billable asks first. Only when the category requires the original work order and none was picked at creation or conversion. Close Work Order stays disabled until a work order or Not in ShopView is picked; Goodwill never shows this. New: an optional Original line select under the original work order; the line sets the original technician for the comeback and warranty numbers (else the lead technician of the original work order). Clicks Close Work Order. Stock parts post to the account of the category (Warranty: 6430). End of flow. Reopen Work Order sits in the invoice menu. The NO CHARGE stamp and Category: Warranty · Original work order S2-30455 sit under the masthead line, clear of the centred logo. On a billable work order, while Internal Work Orders is on and the work order is not invoiced. Same permissions as Convert to No Charge. The item replaces the earlier "Move to a No Charge work order" (dropped Nov 5: a shop that wants it separate splits the work order as today). Clicks Mark as No Charge. Category and Original work order are the same fields as Convert to No Charge; the line stays where it is. New: an optional Original line select under the original work order; the line sets the original technician for the comeback and warranty numbers (else the lead technician of the original work order). The line carries a No Charge · Warranty chip next to its name; Rate, Total and its parts show $0.00, hours and status unchanged. The original work order is in the notes and the Audit Log, not on the line. No badge on the work order: a normal billable work order with one no-charge line. Financial Info is the cost view and does not change: the cost of the no-charge line stays and posts to the Warranty account at invoicing. The marked line offers Change category and Mark as Billable. Mark as Billable prices the line at the customer's current pricing and removes the category. Every line change writes a system note and an Audit Log row: who, when, category, original work order, the price removed, the cost and hours kept. The invoice of a billable work order: no INTERNAL or NO CHARGE stamp, no badge. The no-charge line prints with its hours and parts at $0.00 and one word under the title, Warranty. Totals, tax, deposits and portal approval on the billable amounts. The customer sees zero; the books see the cost: the line's parts cost posts to the Warranty expense account when the invoice is created. Reopen Work Order is in the Finance tab's invoice menu (Flow 2 frame 5). Opens the dialog of frame 2. The Change Customer button is disabled with the tooltip Reopen the work order to change the customer. A billable invoiced work order keeps today's behaviour. Clicks Reopen Work Order. Reopen needs the Work Orders — Delete permission, like Reverse. Classification: No Charge (internal and customer no-charge work). Switches to the Estimates tab. One report for all free work: whole internal and no-charge work orders, and now one row per no-charge line of a billable work order (Line column, Classification "No Charge line", invoiced date). Summary strip per category above the table. Money reports exclude these rows without a filter. Reopen reverses only what was posted; an entry still waiting here gets no reversal and is marked withdrawn. Header and totals only; lines live on the NO CHARGE document in ShopView. Accounts per the AccountingHub owner (Nov 5): 6500 General Internal, 6430 Warranty & Goodwill (existing in the hub chart), Comeback Expense is a new account whose number the hub confirms; migration maps the starting categories automatically, never an empty row for them. Held retries automatically once the row is mapped or the period opened. Dismissed: the Close was withdrawn by Reopen before posting; nothing was posted, so nothing is reversed. Settings > Work Orders. One toggle, Internal Work Orders. Nothing else lives on this tab. First turn-on: pick the internal customers once. Nothing is preselected (the location is not always a customer). Afterwards the flag lives on the customer, not here. Setting on. Two hint lines and a link to the Internal Work Orders page where the categories are managed. Internal categories: General Internal as default plus the shop's own (Company Vehicle Maintenance, Shop Equipment Maintenance). An expense account per category. No Charge categories: Warranty, Goodwill, Comeback to start plus the shop's own (Policy dropped as a default). Third column: requires the original work order (Warranty, Comeback). A category: name, QuickBooks expense account per location, the flag. Archive, never delete; old work orders and reports keep their category. QuickBooks ShopView Accounts: the same mapping, one row per category under Cost of Parts. Edit here or on the category. Nothing is created in QuickBooks; an empty row posts to ShopView Review as today. Customer: Internal customer checkbox plus a Default internal category. Asset of an internal customer: its own internal category. The QuickBooks mark sits in the explanation: categories are mapped to QuickBooks expense accounts. Priority: asset, then customer, then General Internal. New work order for an internal customer: Internal badge, nothing to pick. The category comes from the asset, else the customer, else General Internal; the tooltip names it. Removed after the CEO review: the Internal category select. Pick Forklift 2 and the tooltip names the asset's own category, Shop Equipment Maintenance. New work order for a regular customer with No Charge ticked: Category required (the No Charge list), Original work order when the category requires it, optional here. Three dots on a billable work order: Convert to No Charge. Same permissions as fees and discounts. Convert asks for the category and the original work order. New: an optional Original line select under the original work order; the line sets the original technician for the comeback and warranty numbers (else the lead technician of the original work order). Change category: same two fields. Convert to Billable asks first. Close: the original work order is required for Warranty and Comeback, with Not in ShopView for jobs done before ShopView. The original technician is stored with it. Summary strip per category above the table. Money reports exclude these rows without a filter. AccountingHub Closed record with Classification, Category, Original work order, Original technician. One mapping row per category, seeded. Accounts per the AccountingHub owner (Nov 5): 6500 General Internal, 6430 Warranty & Goodwill (existing in the hub chart), Comeback Expense is a new account whose number the hub confirms; migration maps the starting categories automatically, never an empty row for them. Held names the category row that is not mapped; Dismissed when a Reopen withdraws a Close. v6.1 · Nov 5, 2026 · Internal Work Orders after the CEO review The shop owner turns Internal Work Orders on, picks the company in the modal or later on its customer page, and gets the starting categories. Each category carries its QuickBooks expense account, set on the category like a parts category's Products and Services. v6.1 · Nov 5, 2026 · Internal Work Orders after the CEO review A service advisor repairs one of the shop's own trucks and closes the job without an invoice. States S2 Close Work Order · failed The work order stays Complete. Clicks Close Work Order again. v6.1 · Nov 5, 2026 · Internal Work Orders after the CEO review A work order on a real customer can be converted to no charge, and back, until it is closed or invoiced. It stays on that customer and that asset, closes without an invoice, and its parts cost posts to the expense account of its category (Warranty, Goodwill, Comeback or the shop's own) instead of Cost of Parts. One free line on a paid job is moved to its own No Charge work order (Flow 6); marking a line No Charge in place is V2 and reuses these categories. v6.1 · Nov 5, 2026 · Internal Work Orders after the CEO review A closed internal work order needs a forgotten part, so the service advisor reopens it. This mirrors invoice reversal on external work orders. v6.1 · Nov 5, 2026 · Internal Work Orders after the CEO review A service advisor filters the list down to internal and no-charge work orders, and the Internal Work Orders report shows all free work: whole work orders and single no-charge lines, by category and by original technician. v6.1 · Nov 5, 2026 · Internal Work Orders after the CEO review Nothing is sent as an invoice. The parts cost goes to the mapped expense account; only entries QuickBooks rejects wait here; a missing account posts to ShopView Review. AccountingHub uses the same mapping row and the same hold rule; its held events appear on this page too. A billable work order with a no-charge line reaches the hub as a normal invoice record with a No Charge lines block; the line's parts cost posts to the category account instead of Cost of Parts. v6.1 · Nov 5, 2026 · after the CEO review One free line on a paid job stays on that job. The line is marked No Charge with a category and, where required, the original work order; it shows $0.00 on the work order and the invoice, keeps its hours, parts and story, and its parts cost posts to the category's expense account when the invoice is created. The work order itself stays billable, no badge; Create invoice, pay and close as today. Whole-work-order No Charge (Flow 2) stays for jobs that are entirely free: NO CHARGE document, Closed state. Moving a line to its own work order was dropped: a shop that wants that splits the work order as today. v6.1 · Nov 5, 2026 · Internal Work Orders after the CEO review The happy path, one row per flow, top to bottom: set up, an internal work order to Close, a customer's no-charge work order to Close, one no-charge line on a billable work order, Reopen, finding and reporting, what the books see. Every frame is a copy of its frame on the flow pages; edge cases stay there. v6.1 · Nov 5, 2026 · Review page The screens that changed after the CEO review, in the order a shop meets them: Settings, the categories, where they show up, changing a work order, closing, one no-charge line on a billable work order, finding it and the books, then what was left out on purpose. Every frame is a copy of its Happy flow frame; the number after the dot is the Happy flow frame number. Moving a line to its own work order: dropped (Nov 5) The CEO review settled the line case the other way: a no-charge line stays on the billable work order (row 6). One invoice, the warranty line at $0.00, the rest paid as usual. What that adds to the build: a classification and category per line; $0.00 pricing of the line on the work order, the invoice, the portal and the Finance tab; the line's parts cost posted to the category's account at invoicing; the hub record carrying the line-level category and cost. Whole-work-order No Charge stays as in rows 3 to 5. A shop that wants the free work on its own work order splits the work order as today, then converts it. V2, right after V1: labor posting and technician rates V1 posts the parts cost at Close: a real inventory movement with a known cost. Labor is already paid through payroll, so posting labor on a warranty job means moving a cost out of payroll into the category's account: an internal labor cost per technician, a rule the accountant signs off, and a mapping row per category per kind (parts, labor). V1 already stores the category, the original work order, the original technician and the hours on every internal and no-charge work order and shows them in the report. V2 adds the labor posting and the comeback and warranty rates per technician on top. Doing it in V1 would hold the whole feature for the accounting rule. Separate features, not V1 or V2 Manufacturer warranty as a receivable: claiming the cost back from the manufacturer is a claim process with its own accounting. Retail value of free work on the document or the report: pricing and reporting, no change to classification or posting. Goodwill approval flow: who may give work away for free is permissions and approval, a workflow feature.
